body:
## Problem

Non-primary MCursors render below hlsearch and visual decoration.

## Solution

Implementation:
- Add a `kSHAboveSearch` decoration flag
- Use the above flag for extmarks that're in the `nvim.multicursor{,.*}` namespaces

Closes #41629

## Highlighting Priority

Highlighting priority can't be used - there is a hl priority and a decoration priority concept:
- [HL priority](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/9dd0eeb6eab9c7f070a39b792d93f6ceffe63d4a/runtime/doc/syntax.txt#L3819-L3827): last declared `:hi` wins over other highlights, `syn-keyword` wins over other `syn`s
- Decoration priority is [dealt with separately in `drawline.c` / `win_line()`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/9dd0eeb6eab9c7f070a39b792d93f6ceffe63d4a/src/nvim/decoration.c#L742-L748) and distinguishes [virtual text](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/9dd0eeb6eab9c7f070a39b792d93f6ceffe63d4a/src/nvim/decoration.c#L624) and [sign highlighting](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/9dd0eeb6eab9c7f070a39b792d93f6ceffe63d4a/src/nvim/decoration.c#L644)

Neither hl nor decoration priorities will draw above either search highlighting or area decoration (aka visual mode), which is the source of the bug (see below).

extmark priority only controls ordering between extmarks and doesn't help with decoration priority when it comes to drawing over search-hl/area-decoration.

## Attr selection during screen rendering

The issue is in `win_line()`:

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/9dd0eeb6eab9c7f070a39b792d93f6ceffe63d4a/src/nvim/drawline.c#L2043-L2064

tl;dr:
- Areas are drawn first (visual mode wins over all else)
- Search is drawn next
- Other attributes are drawn after (and otherwise ignored - **this includes extmarks and so mcursors**)

This code must be the one to change, to allow mcursors to render over search-hl and visual mode.

Thanks for the prompt - I hadn't appreciated the detail involved here. I shall explain better and write this up into the PR description when you're happy.

## Highlighting/decoration priorities

Yes, we have a hl priority concept and a decoration priority concept:
- [HL priority](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/9dd0eeb6eab9c7f070a39b792d93f6ceffe63d4a/runtime/doc/syntax.txt#L3819-L3827): last declared `:hi` wins over other highlights, `syn-keyword` wins over other `syn`s
- Decoration priority is [dealt with separately in `drawline.c` / `win_line()`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/9dd0eeb6eab9c7f070a39b792d93f6ceffe63d4a/src/nvim/decoration.c#L742-L748) and distinguishes [virtual text](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/9dd0eeb6eab9c7f070a39b792d93f6ceffe63d4a/src/nvim/decoration.c#L624) and [sign highlighting](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/9dd0eeb6eab9c7f070a39b792d93f6ceffe63d4a/src/nvim/decoration.c#L644)

## Hl/decoration interplay with search-hl and visual mode

Now, neither hl, nor decoration priorities will draw above either search highlighting or area decoration (aka visual mode), which is the source of the bug (see below).

extmark priority only controls ordering between extmarks and doesn't help with decoration priority when it comes to drawing over search-hl/area-decoration.

## The actual drawing colour/attr selection

The issue is in this part of `win_line()`:

https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/9dd0eeb6eab9c7f070a39b792d93f6ceffe63d4a/src/nvim/drawline.c#L2043-L2064

tl;dr:
- Areas are drawn first (visual mode wins over all else)
- Search is drawn next
- Other attributes are drawn after (and otherwise ignored - **this includes extmarks and so mcursors**)

So this is the top-level part of code which decides what wins, and the correct place for "fake"/non-tty cursors to be prioritised. In order to signal this, I've used an attribute on the extmark which propagates through to here, called `above_search`, but it could just as easily be called `render_first` or whatever, to indicate this priority over search and visual decoration.

## z-index

> in fact [#41629 (comment)](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/41629#issuecomment-5514260915) suggests reworking the builtin "always above" to be driven by zindex instead...


I wasn't a fan of zindex, with that implying that something could draw above cursors - a cursor should always be the top-most, so setting a large zindex feels like the wrong approach.

> It might be that `priority` is the right choice here, I always confuse them. I.e. it seems that some built-in ways of adding highlight (search, spelling, `:match`) have the highest priority-and-or-zindex compared to extmarks.

Yes, you've got it exactly - there's a builtin way of some having more prioritised than others, despite any `priority` or highlight ordering.

> I wasn't a fan of zindex, with that implying that something could draw above cursors - a cursor should always be the top-most

If that's the case, we can just special-case the `nvim.multicursor` extmarks internally, for now at least. I think priority/zindex is the long-term preference.

> we can just special-case the `nvim.multicursor` extmarks internally, for now at least. I think priority/zindex is the long-term preference.

Consider it done - the namespace is now used to infer the search-hl/visual-mode override, no changes to extmark API

[Test change](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/compare/b85d6139f03f168ff3331bab91441773afdb0fd3..480f553add7b8e14e00dc142c95d96ccbd200600) feels hacky, but then I suppose it is checking for namespaces which could change as a side-effect, given they're lazy.
